title: Anyone can frontrun a funded nudge balance by calling batchMint with their own recipient
description: The nudge payout uses `IERC20(_nudgeTokenEntry).balanceOf(address(this))` — i.e. the entire current balance — as the payout amount, with no per-batch cap or per-user accounting. Any caller who satisfies `count >= nudgeSize` and pays for that many mints sweeps the full pool to whichever `recipient` they pass. Once a yield-funnel deposits NUDGE into the contract, an MEV searcher can see the deposit in the mempool and immediately submit a `batchMint` with `count == nudgeSize` (the minimum qualifying batch) and `recipient = themselves`, capturing the entire deposit for the price of `nudgeSize` mints. The intended user (whose larger batch was supposed to earn the incentive) gets nothing. The contract's NatSpec acknowledges that pre-funded balances 'simply donate to the next caller' but does not acknowledge that the next caller can be an unrelated frontrunner with the minimum qualifying batch.
exploit_scenario: 1) The yield funnel deposits 10,000 USDC of nudge into BatchNFTMinter, intending to incentivise large batches (`nudgeSize = 100`). 2) Alice prepares `batchMint(..., count = 1000, recipient = Alice, paymentAmount = X)` — she expects to qualify for the nudge because 1000 >= 100. 3) Mallory's bot sees the funnel's deposit, immediately submits `batchMint(..., count = 100, recipient = Mallory, paymentAmount = small)` with higher gas. 4) Mallory's tx lands first, sweeps all 10,000 USDC to Mallory for the cost of 100 mints. Alice's tx lands next, finds `balanceOf(this) == 0` for the nudge, mints 1000 NFTs as a normal batch with no incentive.
recommended_mitigation: Pay a fixed per-batch nudge amount (owner-set), capped at the current balance, rather than always sweeping the full balance. Alternatively scale the payout by `count` (e.g. `nudgeAmount * (count / nudgeSize)` capped at balance) so attackers with the minimum qualifying batch can only claim a proportional slice. As a third option, restrict the nudge to a whitelisted relayer set (the actual yield funnel address) by gating the qualifying call on `msg.sender`.
notes: This is the canonical 'first-come-first-serve sweep' antipattern. The recipient/msg.sender split makes it worse: msg.sender pays the mint cost but recipient receives the nudge, so an attacker can sandwich a legitimate user's funding event without ever touching the funded token.
